knowledge:
- key_parameters: data_as_input=Path to raw data, or a dataframe/matrix, or a SummarizedExperiment object ;; description_as_input=Path to description file, or a dataframe/matrix (not needed if using SummarizedExperiment with batch info) ;; algorithm=Batch correction algorithm, either "ComBat" (default) or "limma" ;; ComBat_mode=Integer (1 to 4) specifying ComBat arguments (default is 1) ;; plot=Set to "samplemeans", "featuremeans", or "CV" to generate boxplots of pre- and post-adjusted data ;; output_file=Name/path of the output .tsv file (defaults to "cured_data"). Set to FALSE to disable ;; sort=Sorting algorithm prior to adjustment ("sparcity_sort", "seriation_sort", or "jaccard_sort") ;; block=Integer dictating how many batches to pack together during matrix dissection ;; verbosity=Integer controlling command line feedback (0 or "mute" to silence, 1 is default) ;; cores=Number of cores to use (defaults to all available cores) ;; ur=Logical (TRUE/FALSE) to toggle unique removal for increased feature rescue (default is TRUE)
- alternatives: Standard ComBat (from sva) or limma directly, which are unable to deal with missing data points on their own.
- when_to_use: When performing batch effect correction on high-throughput biological data (especially proteomics) that contains missing values (NA).
- pitfalls: Trying to plot data using the plot parameter when the data has not been log-transformed prior to running HarmonizR may lead to an unplottable result ;; The sort parameter does not yield any benefit when the block parameter is unused ;; ComBat_mode is only valid when algorithm is set to "ComBat".

workflows.name: batch_correction_dataframe
workflows.intent: Perform batch effect correction on a data frame containing missing values using ComBat or limma.
input: df (a data frame or matrix of molecular features, e.g., proteins or genes, with samples as columns and features as rows)
des (a description data frame mapping sample IDs to their respective batches)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare the input data frame and sample description data frame ;; 2. Run the harmonizR function to perform matrix dissection and batch effect correction.
workflows.code:
df <- data.frame(matrix(rnorm(n = 3*6), ncol = 6))
colnames(df) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F")
row_names <- c("F1", "F2", "F3")
rownames(df) <- row_names
batch <- rep(1:3, each = 2)
des <- data.frame(ID = colnames(df), sample = 1:6, batch = batch)
result <- harmonizR(df, des, output_file = FALSE, cores = 1)
